methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 575 advanced lung adenocarcinoma patients with 26 clinical variables analyzed using multivariable Cox regression and five ML survival models. The authors apply appropriate methods for censored time-to-event data, including the TSHRC test when proportional hazards may be violated and collinearity diagnostics (Belsley-Kuh-Welsch). However, patients with missing data are simply excluded from multivariable analysis rather than imputed, no power calculation is given, only 70/30 random splits are used for ML validation (no external validation cohort), and selection bias is only briefly acknowledged for the bevacizumab line-of-therapy analysis. Statistical reporting includes hazard ratios with 95% CIs and log-rank P-values but effect sizes for many subgroup comparisons are absent.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is a single-center retrospective chart review that confirms several well-known associations (EGFR mutation benefit, afatinib vs first-generation TKI differences, bevacizumab combination benefit) in a Taiwanese cohort from 2010-2019. It is clinically plausible but does not change practice; the authors themselves note that osimertinib (current first-line standard in many settings) was unavailable in their data. The ML models achieve only moderate discrimination (best C-index ~0.70) with no external validation, limiting translational utility. Classified as Oxford LoE 4 as a retrospective observational cohort without a matched or prospective control comparison.

reporting_quality.justification: The study is a retrospective observational cohort to which STROBE applies; most core STROBE items are present (setting, participants, variables, statistical methods, descriptive table of participants, main results with effect estimates) but key items are underreported: no flow diagram, inclusion/exclusion criteria are minimal ('no other specific inclusion or exclusion criteria'), and handling of missing data is only a one-line mention. The ML portion also partially invokes TRIPOD territory but provides limited calibration, no external validation, and no prediction model presentation (no equation, no shared model weights). No data-sharing statement is identifiable and code is not released, warranting a data availability score of 1.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper largely confirms established findings (EGFR status prognostic value, afatinib vs first-generation TKIs, bevacizumab combination benefit, PD-L1 and OS). The ML comparison across five survival models on 26 features is moderately novel in this specific Taiwanese cohort, but the broader approach (Cox, RSF, GBS, SVM, decision tree for NSCLC prognosis) has been published previously, including reference 28 on early-stage NSCLC. The authors frame the C-index dynamic assessment as innovative but do not demonstrate a methodological advance beyond standard scikit-survival usage.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable and generally well-organized into standard IMRaD sections. However, there are notable issues: inconsistent EGFR variant counts (n=229 vs 218 in text but subgroup totals differ), a stray mention of bevacizumab use in ovarian cancer in the Discussion that is off-topic for the lung cohort, minor typos (e.g., 'erotinib', 'permetrexed'), and Table/Figure descriptions that are sometimes sparse. Figures are referenced but the manuscript text alone does not always make interpretation straightforward without seeing them.

key_strengths: Decade-long single-institution cohort of 575 advanced lung adenocarcinoma patients with harmonized EGFR, ALK, PD-L1 and treatment data
Appropriate use of TSHRC two-stage test when proportional hazards may be violated (e.g., bevacizumab analysis)
Systematic comparison of five survival ML models with C-index and time-dependent AUC
Clinically meaningful observation of afatinib OS advantage over gefitinib/erlotinib within their cohort
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with no external validation of the ML models; best C-index only ~0.70
Missing data handled by exclusion; no imputation or sensitivity analyses described
Absence of osimertinib era data limits contemporary clinical relevance
No data or code availability statement; TRIPOD items largely unreported for the prediction model
Several comparisons (PD-L1 strata, rare EGFR variants, bevacizumab line) are underpowered with very small subgroups
Inconsistent subgroup counts and minor textual errors suggest limited copy-editing
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent but incremental single-center retrospective NSCLC study with moderate ML discrimination and limited novelty; appropriate for a mid-tier oncology journal (tier 3) after major revisions addressing external validation, missing data, and reporting completeness.
